prompt: A model cube is rebuilt with every edge $3$ times as long. The surface area of the new cube is how many times the surface area of the original?
hint: Surface area is built from two dimensions, so scaling hits it twice.

hints.text: Surface area is built from two dimensions, so scaling hits it twice.
Test it: a cube of edge $1$ has surface area $6$; a cube of edge $3$ has surface area $6(3^2) = 54$.

explanation: If every length is multiplied by $k$, area is multiplied by $k^2$ and volume by $k^3$.
Here $k = 3$, so surface area grows by $3^2 = 9$.
The new cube has $9$ times the surface area (and $27$ times the volume).

alternativeExplanations.title: Look at one face
steps: One face goes from a $1$-by-$1$ square to a $3$-by-$3$ square — that is $9$ little squares instead of $1$.
All six faces grow the same way, so the whole surface is $9$ times bigger.
